front: How does 3D echo compare to 2D biplane Simpson's for LV volume measurement?
back: 3D reduces geometric assumptions and foreshortening — volumes are LARGER than 2D biplane and closer to cMRI (though still slightly smaller than cMRI). EF values are similar across modalities.

front: State the ASE definition of LV concentric remodeling vs concentric hypertrophy.
back: Both have RWT > 0.42. Concentric remodeling: NORMAL LV mass index. Concentric hypertrophy: INCREASED LV mass index (> 102 g/m² men, > 88 g/m² women).

front: Which strain reduction defines subclinical cardiotoxicity from chemotherapy?
back: A relative reduction in global longitudinal strain > 15% from baseline. Detects dysfunction before LVEF declines.

front: How does the RVOT PW envelope's mid-systolic notching relate to pulmonary hypertension?
back: Mid-systolic notching of the RVOT/PA velocity envelope indicates severe pulmonary hypertension — transient reversal of the RVOT-PA gradient from poor PA compliance.

front: What is Simpson's biplane method's main limitation and how do you avoid it?
back: Foreshortening — cutting off the true LV apex on apical views underestimates volume. Avoid by using extended-focus or off-axis views to visualize the true apex, or use 3D echo.

front: Name three techniques to improve endocardial border definition when calculating LV volumes.
back: 1) Harmonic imaging. 2) LV opacification with IV contrast (when ≥ 2 basal/mid segments poorly seen). 3) Reduce depth to focus on LV. 4) Use appropriate gain and TGC.

front: How does 3D echo directly measure LV mass?
back: By directly measuring the volume of myocardium between the endocardial and epicardial surfaces × specific gravity of muscle (1.05). No geometric assumption is required. Correlates well with cMRI.

front: How is the LV shape ('sphericity index') described in dilated cardiomyopathy?
back: DCM: LV becomes more spherical (short-axis/long-axis ratio approaches 1). Normal LV is more elliptical (short/long axis ratio ~0.5). Sphericity worsens as remodeling progresses.

front: For LVOT PW measurement, why should the sample volume be 2–3 mm proximal to the aortic valve?
back: Placing the PW too close captures the acceleration into the AV. Placing too far captures LV inflow. 2–3 mm proximal gives a clean laminar signal. An audible AV closure click on the trace indicates the sample volume is at the valve level.

front: Which single measure of contractility is preload- AND afterload-independent?
back: End-systolic elastance (Ees) — the slope of the end-systolic pressure-volume relationship. Not routinely measured on echo. Strain rate is a practical noninvasive analogue.
